variants.title: State the contract
variants.context: A completion is a temporary proposal attached to one exact cursor state. Typing never waits for completion; generated text never enters the document without an explicit user action; returning no suggestion is a normal, healthy outcome.
variants.prompt: The service is slow and the editor pauses keystrokes while waiting. What rule is broken?
options: Nothing; a short pause is fine.
optionFeedback: The writer owns the document and can keep typing at any moment.
Deadlines exist to protect this rule.
variants.explanation: Do not make editing depend on model, ranking, policy, or telemetry availability.

variants.title: State the contract
variants.context: A completion is a temporary proposal attached to one exact cursor state. Typing never waits for completion; generated text never enters the document without an explicit user action; returning no suggestion is a normal, healthy outcome.
variants.prompt: A completion is auto-inserted when the writer pauses for two seconds. What is wrong?
options: Generated text must never enter the document without an explicit user action.
Nothing, because a two-second pause is a clear signal that the writer consents.
The pause threshold should be raised to five seconds before auto-insertion.
optionFeedback: Acceptance uses an explicit key, gesture, or selection.
Silence is not acceptance. A writer who paused to think has agreed to nothing.
Duration does not create consent. A longer wait only makes the same unrequested edit rarer.
variants.explanation: Keep ordinary typing, undo, and input-method composition authoritative.

variants.title: State the contract
variants.context: A completion is a temporary proposal attached to one exact cursor state. Typing never waits for completion; generated text never enters the document without an explicit user action; returning no suggestion is a normal, healthy outcome.
variants.prompt: Suggestion coverage is being optimized upward as a success metric. What is the risk?
options: Latency improves, because the model stops filtering out low-scoring candidates.
A weak suggestion consumes attention even when ignored, so restraint is lost.
No real risk, since a writer can ignore any suggestion at no cost.
optionFeedback: Coverage and latency are unrelated. Showing more candidates makes no request faster.
Restraint is part of the product.
Reading and dismissing a bad suggestion costs attention, the scarcest resource while writing.
variants.hint: What does an ignored suggestion cost the writer?
variants.explanation: Do not optimize suggestion coverage as if more visible text were always better.

variants.title: Qualify locally
variants.context: The client eliminates requests locally: confirm the feature and personalization mode are enabled; require enough non-whitespace prefix; exclude sensitive fields; pause during composition or rapid cursor movement; debounce and cancel superseded versions; back off on overload.
variants.prompt: A keystroke arrives in the editor. Put the client’s eligibility checks in order.

items.text: Exclude password, payment, and other sensitive fields before any network work.
Apply client backoff if the service reports overload.
Confirm the feature and any personalization mode are enabled for this account and surface.
Require enough non-whitespace prefix to infer a continuation.
Pause during input-method composition, multi-cursor edits, or rapid cursor movement.
Debounce recent typing and cancel work for superseded draft versions.

variants.hint: Sensitive fields are excluded before anything leaves the device.
variants.explanation: Local qualification protects privacy, saves capacity, and keeps the model out of every keystroke.

variants.title: Qualify locally
variants.context: The client eliminates requests locally: confirm the feature and personalization mode are enabled; require enough non-whitespace prefix; exclude sensitive fields; pause during composition or rapid cursor movement; debounce and cancel superseded versions; back off on overload.
variants.prompt: A password field gains focus. Put the checks in order, showing where the request stops.

items.text: No debounce needed.
No backoff needed.
Sensitive field: excluded; no request is made.
Prefix long enough: possibly.
Feature enabled: yes.
No composition check needed.

variants.hint: The exclusion happens before network work.
variants.explanation: Measure the percentage of editor states rejected by each reason.

variants.context: The client eliminates requests locally: confirm the feature and personalization mode are enabled; require enough non-whitespace prefix; exclude sensitive fields; pause during composition or rapid cursor movement; debounce and cancel superseded versions; back off on overload.
variants.prompt: The service reports repeated deadline misses. Put the checks in order, ending with the response to overload.

items.text: Sufficient prefix.
Client backoff reduces request frequency.
Not composing.
Debounced and superseded versions cancelled.
Feature enabled.
Not a sensitive field.

variants.hint: Backoff is the client’s part of overload control.
variants.explanation: A client regression must not silently multiply serving demand.

variants.title: Cross the boundaries
variants.context: A candidate crosses independent boundaries: the client debounces, captures cursor and draft versions, and builds the smallest context; the service picks a tier, decodes bounded candidates, and stops at the deadline; ranking combines relevance with policy, repetition, language, and freshness gates; ghost text shows only if the draft version still matches and inserts only on accept.
variants.prompt: A request is eligible. Put the candidate’s path in order.

items.text: Ghost text is shown only if the draft version still matches, and inserted only after the writer accepts.
The client debounces, captures cursor and draft versions, and builds the smallest permitted context envelope.
Ranking combines relevance with policy, repetition, language, freshness, and product thresholds.
The service chooses a model tier, decodes a bounded number of continuations, and stops when the deadline is unreachable.

variants.hint: Every request is correlated with one draft version.
variants.explanation: The client may discard the response even after every server-side gate passes.

variants.title: Cross the boundaries
variants.context: A candidate crosses independent boundaries: the client debounces, captures cursor and draft versions, and builds the smallest context; the service picks a tier, decodes bounded candidates, and stops at the deadline; ranking combines relevance with policy, repetition, language, and freshness gates; ghost text shows only if the draft version still matches and inserts only on accept.
variants.prompt: The writer keeps typing while a request is in flight. Put the path in order, ending with what happens to the response.

items.text: Ranking passed a candidate.
The request carried draft version 41.
The client sees the draft is now version 42 and discards the response.
The service decoded candidates.

variants.hint: Freshness is decided on the client.
variants.explanation: A response for an old draft must never appear on a newer draft.

variants.title: Cross the boundaries
variants.context: A candidate crosses independent boundaries: the client debounces, captures cursor and draft versions, and builds the smallest context; the service picks a tier, decodes bounded candidates, and stops at the deadline; ranking combines relevance with policy, repetition, language, and freshness gates; ghost text shows only if the draft version still matches and inserts only on accept.
variants.prompt: The primary tier cannot meet the deadline. Put the path in order with the fallback.

items.text: Ranking gates whatever candidate exists.
The service detects the primary tier cannot finish in time and returns no suggestion or an approved simpler candidate.
The client sends the smallest context with a deadline.
The client shows nothing or the fallback, never a late result.

variants.hint: Returning nothing is a valid path.
variants.explanation: Reject work that cannot finish before its result becomes useful.

variants.title: Rank with gates
variants.context: Generation answers what is plausible; ranking answers whether any candidate is worth showing. A weighted score orders candidates but must not average away a failed hard gate. The reject option is first-class.
variants.prompt: A candidate scores highest on relevance but violates the surface’s policy. What happens?
options: It is shown with a warning label so the writer can decide for themselves.
It is suppressed; a weighted score must not average away a failed hard gate.
It is shown, because the weighted score puts relevance above the policy term.
optionFeedback: A policy failure is not a disclosure problem. The candidate should never reach the surface.
Averaging lets a strong relevance score outvote a violation, which hard gates exist to stop.
variants.hint: Is policy a weight or a gate?
variants.explanation: Combine evidence, then apply hard gates.

variants.title: Rank with gates
variants.context: Generation answers what is plausible; ranking answers whether any candidate is worth showing. A weighted score orders candidates but must not average away a failed hard gate. The reject option is first-class.
variants.prompt: Why keep generation and ranking separate?
options: They are the same step, since the highest-probability candidate is the one to show.
Ranking is faster, so running it separately keeps the generator off the typing path.
So policy and thresholds can change without retraining the generator.
optionFeedback: Plausible text is not the same as text worth interrupting for. Those are different questions.
Speed is not the reason. Ranking is separate so the show-or-suppress policy can change alone.
Generation answers plausibility; ranking answers whether to interrupt.
variants.hint: Which question does each component answer?
variants.explanation: Ranking must earn the right to interrupt.

variants.title: Rank with gates
variants.context: Generation answers what is plausible; ranking answers whether any candidate is worth showing. A weighted score orders candidates but must not average away a failed hard gate. The reject option is first-class.
variants.prompt: The candidate only echoes the two characters the writer would type next. Which gate fails?
options: Freshness: the draft moved on since the request.
Language: the candidate is in the wrong locale.
Utility: it does not save meaningful work.
optionFeedback: The draft is current, so freshness passes. The problem is what the suggestion is worth.
The language matches the surrounding text. Nothing about the locale failed here.
Suggestions must save work, not echo the obvious.
variants.hint: How much work does the suggestion save?
variants.explanation: The reject option is a first-class behavior.

variants.title: Budget the interaction
variants.context: The Gmail Smart Compose paper reported a p90 end-to-end requirement below 60 ms for that system. Allocate a budget across every stage; propagate an absolute deadline; degrade by reducing frequency, context, candidates, or tier before queues grow.
variants.prompt: The end-to-end budget is 60 ms. Client debounce uses 10 ms, network 20 ms, and inference 20 ms. How many milliseconds remain for ranking gates and rendering?
variants.hint: Subtract each stage from the budget.
variants.explanation: 60 − 10 − 20 − 20 = 10 ms for gates and render; record each stage separately.

mistakes.feedback: Every stage consumes part of the budget.

variants.title: Budget the interaction
variants.context: The Gmail Smart Compose paper reported a p90 end-to-end requirement below 60 ms for that system. Allocate a budget across every stage; propagate an absolute deadline; degrade by reducing frequency, context, candidates, or tier before queues grow.
variants.prompt: Fleet-wide, editors produce 1,000 keystrokes per second and local eligibility rejects 70% of states. How many requests per second reach the service?
variants.explanation: 1,000 × 0.30 = 300 requests per second; a client regression in eligibility would multiply this.

variants.title: Budget the interaction
variants.context: The Gmail Smart Compose paper reported a p90 end-to-end requirement below 60 ms for that system. Allocate a budget across every stage; propagate an absolute deadline; degrade by reducing frequency, context, candidates, or tier before queues grow.
variants.prompt: 300 requests per second each decode 4 bounded candidates. How many candidates per second does ranking evaluate?
variants.hint: Multiply requests by candidates per request.
variants.explanation: 300 × 4 = 1,200 candidates per second before hard gates suppress most of them.
